extensionDescription.message: Checks lookalike hostname characters and five visual spelling patterns against registered domains.

permissionNote.message: Leave unchecked to allow it only in this tab.

settingsIntro.message: These hostnames bypass warnings. They are saved when you select “Always allow this hostname” on a warning and continue. Both the basic character check and the additional similarity check are bypassed while permission is active. Remove an entry to check it again on the next visit. Tab-only permissions do not appear here.

emptyList.message: No saved hostnames. To add one, select “Always allow this hostname” on the warning page and continue.

storageNote.message: Allowed sites and your domain list changes are stored in this Chrome profile on this device. They are not sent elsewhere or synced to other devices.

removalNote.message: Removing a hostname also revokes its tab-only permissions. Pages that are already open will stay open.

noHostnameNote.message: Character differences appear here when a hostname needs your attention.

searchStopped.message: The search results have been hidden.

accessStopped.message: Navigation to this hostname was blocked.

reopenURL.message: Open the original URL again before choosing whether to continue.

warningUnavailable.message: Could not verify this warning. Open the original URL again.

permissionRemoved.message: Removed permission for “$1”. It will be checked the next time you open it.

checkCharacters.message: Check the character differences before continuing.

listBackgroundFailed.message: Could not update allowed sites. Please try again.

pendingMissing.message: This warning has expired. Open the original URL again.

permissionInvalid.message: Could not verify the permission setting.

continueRetry.message: Could not continue. Please try again.

similarDomainReason.message: This hostname resembles a registered domain for $1 ($2). Similarity alone does not mean it is a fake site.

protectionIntro.message: Register genuine domains of companies and services whose impersonators you want to detect here. The 143 included domains are checked automatically without setup.

protectionPatterns.message: The following substitutions are checked. These are illustrative examples of visual confusion, not reports of actual incidents. A warning appears when a destination resembles a registered genuine domain.

protectionInputHelp.message: Example: amazon.com. Enter genuine ASCII domains verified on the official website, not fake domains. Separate multiple domains with commas or new lines. Do not include https://, a URL path or wildcard (*).

protectionSaveFailed.message: Could not save the domain list. Your previous settings have been kept. Try again.

protectionInvalid.message: Enter a name and valid ASCII domain names, without a scheme, path, port, credentials or wildcard.

protectionDuplicate.message: This domain is already registered. Edit its existing entry.

protectionLimit.message: You can register up to 200 companies/services and 400 domains.

protectionRuleFailed.message: Chrome could not create a blocking rule for these domains. Your previous settings have been kept.

protectionListPurpose.message: This list supplies reference domains for an additional check of lookalike combinations made from ordinary letters and digits. Destinations are compared with the registered domains using five patterns: rn/m, 0/o, 1/l/i (I), vv/w and cl/d.

protectionListScope.message: Cyrillic characters and listed non-ASCII lookalike letters are checked even when a destination is not on this list. Hostnames you have allowed bypass checks while that permission is active.

protectionListEdit.message: Add companies and services you use in the fields above. Edit or remove existing entries in the list below. To skip warnings and permit a destination, use the separate Allowed sites list.

mainFunctionIntro.message: NoKiridding checks destination domain names for Cyrillic characters and listed non-ASCII letters that resemble ordinary Latin letters. When it finds a target character, it blocks navigation and highlights the character with an explanation.

mainFunctionScope.message: This basic check works without registering sites in a list. It checks the domain name, including subdomains and endings such as .com. URL paths and query strings are outside the check.

optionalSettingsIntro.message: In addition to the basic feature above, this feature checks deceptive combinations of letters and digits, and names added around registered domain names. Because there are countless possible targets, 101 companies whose names may be impersonated in phishing are included. Add more using the fields below.

mainFunctionExample.message: The lower example replaces the first Latin letter “a” with the similar-looking Cyrillic letter “а”. The highlighted character is not a Latin letter, so NoKiridding stops navigation and shows a warning.

patternRnExample.message: rn / m: amazon → arnazon. Adjacent r and n can resemble m.

patternZeroExample.message: 0 / o: google → g00gle. The digit 0 replaces the letter o.

patternOneExample.message: 1 / l / i (I): paypal → paypa1. The digit 1 or uppercase I can resemble lowercase l. Lowercase i is also compared.

patternVvExample.message: vv / w: windows → vvindovvs. Two adjacent v letters can resemble w.

patternClExample.message: cl / d: adobe → aclobe. Adjacent c and l can resemble d.

patternCaseNote.message: About uppercase I: Chrome lowercases domain names, so an entered I is compared as i with the digit 1 and lowercase l. The visual resemblance depends on the font.

brandDomainReason.message: This differs from a registered official domain for $1 ($2). This does not prove it is a phishing site.

brandDifference.message: Added or different parts of the main name and its suffix are highlighted in red.

brandCheckHelp.message: For example, support-mercari.com or mercari-support.com can trigger a warning against the registered mercari.com. The main name and its suffix, such as .com, are compared. Prefixes such as jp. are outside this additional check. Unregistered official domains and commentary sites can also trigger warnings, so this does not prove phishing. You can still Continue.
